front.title: Minimum Public Discovery Information: Requirements and Common Semantics

abstract.t:
The charter of the Discovery of Agents With Names (DAWN) working group asks it to specify the minimum public discovery information that a client obtains when it discovers an AI resource. An individual draft on DAWN terminology defines Minimum Discoverable Information (MDI) as the minimum amount of information an entity needs to provide to become discoverable, distinguishes it from the Minimum Viable Dataset (MVD) that a discovery mechanism needs as input, and gives only examples of the content of either. Individual drafts on the DAWN problem statement and requirements call for a standardized minimum structure and list what it must at least contain; in its absence, emerging discovery formats risk each defining its own minimal metadata, with descriptors that do not interoperate across organizational or protocol boundaries.
This document addresses the minimum public discovery information as a client obtains it and as a publisher provides it, and its relation to the input of discovery; registration mechanisms are outside its scope. Using the distinction RFC 3444 draws between information models and data models, it describes the information involved in publication, lookup, and response; proposes a procedure that derives what is minimal for each deployment context from the scope of the charter; applies the procedure to the charter's three deployment contexts: a local network, an organization, and the domain of a cooperating party; and proposes a set of elements with the minimal constraints that hold among them. Information can be supplied by the discovery response, by context the client already has, or by binding rules. This document is input to the DAWN architecture and protocol work; normative definitions that affect interoperability belong to the corresponding Standards Track documents. It is a mapping target for richer descriptors.
